/en/airport-assistance/: Search flight, airport and airline help records across ten countries: find airlines like Thai Airways by name or code, airport counters and contacts, and what to keep if a bag is missing.
/en/airport-assistance/airports/: Thailand airport guides for Suvarnabhumi (BKK), Don Mueang (DMK), Phuket (HKT) and Chiang Mai (CNX): arrival, departure and facility guidance, plus help when a flight is delayed or a bag is lost.
/en/airport-assistance/airports/bkk/: Suvarnabhumi Airport guide: how arrivals and departures work, Doors versus Gates, concourses A–G and SAT-1, AOT Limousine and rental cars on Level 2, and the Airport Rail Link on B1. Enquiries: 1722.
/en/airport-assistance/airports/bkk/map/: Suvarnabhumi Airport indoor maps: browse the main terminal, concourses A–G and SAT-1 floor by floor, and search ATMs, currency exchange, prayer rooms and shops. Map codes are not gate numbers.
/en/airport-assistance/airports/bkk/smok: Suvarnabhumi Airport smoking areas: public smoking rooms outside Doors 1 and 10 on Levels 2 and 4, and a visitor-reported room after immigration near Burger King in Concourse D.
/en/airport-assistance/airports/bkk/tran: Suvarnabhumi Airport to Bangkok: compare the Airport Rail Link (35–45 baht to Phaya Thai), public taxis with a 50-baht surcharge plus tolls, and Grab or Bolt pickups at Door 4 on Level 1.
/en/airport-assistance/airports/cnx/: Chiang Mai International Airport (CNX) guide: follow Domestic and International signs, find the 24-hour Grab service centre on domestic Level 1 and the airport shuttle at Door 12. Open 06:00–24:00.
/en/airport-assistance/airports/dmk/: Don Mueang International Airport (DMK) guide: Terminal 1 handles international flights and Terminal 2 domestic ones. Use floor maps to find shops, banks and ATMs; the airport operates 24 hours.
/en/airport-assistance/airports/hkt/: Phuket International Airport (HKT) guide: separate international and domestic terminals, the international arrivals hall on Level 1 with baggage belts 1–5, and self-check-in kiosks on Level 3.
/en/attractions/ancient-city-muang-boran: Muang Boran (Ancient City) in Samut Prakan is an outdoor museum of Thai palace and temple architecture. Open daily 09:00–19:00; international entry is 800 baht, with car entry charged extra.
/en/attractions/aquaria-phuket/: Aquaria Phuket is an indoor aquarium on B1 of Central Phuket Floresta, with otters, penguins, rays and a large marine tank. Open 11:00–19:00; buy online tickets at least three hours ahead.
/en/attractions/ayutthaya-historical-par: Ayutthaya Historical Park covers the ruins of Siam’s old capital, a UNESCO site destroyed in 1767. See how Wat Mahathat and Wat Phra Si Sanphet differ, and why entry is handled site by site.
/en/attractions/bangsaen-aquarium/: Bangsaen Aquarium at Burapha University’s Institute of Marine Science shows Thai sea life by habitat. Open 09:00–16:00 except Mondays, with diver feeding at 14:30 and daily touch-pool sessions.
/en/attractions/bophut-fishermans-villag: Bophut Fisherman’s Village is a coast road on Koh Samui’s north shore where old Chinese wooden shophouses now hold shops, rooms and seafood restaurants, with hand-carved soap and crafts to browse.
/en/attractions/bridge-over-river-kwai/: The Bridge Over the River Kwai in Kanchanaburi is a working bridge on the Thailand–Burma Railway, built by prisoners of war in 1942–1943. See how it differs from the film and how to visit safely.
/en/attractions/bueng-boraphet-aquarium/: Bueng Boraphet Aquarium is a separate building in the Nakhon Sawan lake tourism complex, with a 24-metre freshwater tunnel and over 33 tanks of freshwater, marine and non-local species.
/en/attractions/bueng-chawak-aquarium/: Bueng Chawak Aquarium in Suphan Buri splits its exhibits by building: a freshwater tunnel in Building 2 and a marine tunnel with rays, sea turtles and a shark tank in Building 3. Opens 08:30 daily.
/en/attractions/categories/markets/: Compare 12 night markets and markets in Thailand, from Chatuchak and Or Tor Kor in Bangkok to the Amphawa and Khlong Lat Mayom floating markets. Filter by region and spot the weekend-only ones.
/en/attractions/categories/temples/: Browse 30 temples in Thailand, from Wat Pho’s Reclining Buddha and Wat Arun to the ruins of Ayutthaya and Sukhothai. Filter by region and tell active places of worship from archaeological sites.
/en/attractions/categories/theme-water-p: Compare six theme parks and water parks in Thailand, including Siam Amazing Park, Dream World, Andamanda Phuket and Ramayana Water Park. Note that ride height limits still apply to child tickets.
/en/attractions/charoen-krung/: Charoen Krung is Bangkok’s old riverside commercial road, now home to TCDC in the Central Post Office and Warehouse 30’s seven wartime warehouses. Plan which buildings to visit, as they are separate.
/en/attractions/chatuchak-market/: Chatuchak Weekend Market in Bangkok opens Saturday and Sunday 09:00–18:00. Find clothing in Sections 2–4, vintage in 5–6 and art in 7, plus the Thursday–Friday plant section and nearby stations.
/en/attractions/chiang-mai-night-bazaar/: Chiang Mai Night Bazaar is an evening shopping district on Chang Khlan Road, listed as open daily from about 16:00 to 23:30. See how it differs from the weekend walking streets and Anusarn Market.
/en/attractions/chiang-mai-night-safari/: Chiang Mai Night Safari has two vehicle routes: Savanna Safari with giraffes and zebras, and Predator Prowl with tigers and lions, plus walking exhibits and shows. It is separate from Chiang Mai Zoo.
/en/attractions/chiang-mai-zoo/: Chiang Mai Zoo sits at the foot of Doi Suthep with capybaras, kangaroos and penguins. Adult admission is 350 baht; the aquarium needs a separate ticket, and golf carts cost 350 baht per hour.
/en/attractions/damnoen-saduak-floating-: Damnoen Saduak Floating Market in Ratchaburi is about two hours from Bangkok, with fruit and noodle boats on Khlong Ton Khem. Arrive by around 09:00 to see the morning trade, on foot or by boat.
/en/attractions/erawan-museum/: Erawan Museum in Samut Prakan is crowned by a giant three-headed elephant. Explore three levels of antiques, a stained-glass ceiling and Buddha images; open daily 09:00–18:00, adult entry 500 baht.
/en/attractions/jim-thompson-house/: Jim Thompson House Museum in Bangkok is the silk entrepreneur’s canal-side home of six teak houses and Asian art. Visits are guided, open daily 10:00–17:00, a short walk from BTS National Stadium.
/en/attractions/khao-kheow-open-zoo/: Khao Kheow Open Zoo in Si Racha, Chonburi, is home of the pygmy hippo Moo Deng. Open 08:00–17:00 with adult entry at 350 baht; check penguin parade and elephant swimming times and in-zoo transport.
/en/attractions/khao-san-road/: Khao San Road is a roughly 300-metre backpacker street in Bangkok’s Old Town with hostels, hotels, bars and food from pad Thai to falafel. Sam Yot MRT is the nearest station; expect lively nights.
/en/attractions/khlong-lat-mayom-floatin: Khlong Lat Mayom Floating Market in western Bangkok runs on weekends and public holidays, 08:00–17:00. Eat grilled fish, boat noodles and khanom ko by the canal without needing to board a boat.
/en/attractions/mae-klong-railway-market: Mae Klong Railway Market in Samut Songkhram is where vendors fold their awnings as trains pass. See Mae Klong Station train times, free entry and the train–ferry–train route from Bangkok.
/en/attractions/museum-siam/: Museum Siam in Bangkok explores Thai identity through food, clothing and everyday objects, with hands-on displays. Open Tuesday–Sunday 10:00–18:00, admission 100 baht, by Exit 1 of Sanam Chai MRT.
/en/attractions/nakhon-ratchasima-zoo/: Nakhon Ratchasima Zoo (Korat Zoo) has an African savanna-style landscape with giraffes, lions and white rhinos. Foreign adults pay 350 baht; shuttles, golf carts and bicycles are charged separately.
/en/attractions/national-museum-bangkok/: National Museum Bangkok shows Thai history, Buddhist art and royal funeral chariots in the former Front Palace. Entry is 240 baht; closed Mondays, Tuesdays and public holidays.
/en/attractions/nimmanhaemin/: Nimmanhaemin in Chiang Mai is a neighbourhood of cafés, galleries and boutiques along a 1 km road and its sois. Find craft shops on Soi 1, a gallery café on Soi 17 and the One Nimman complex.
/en/attractions/nong-khai-aquarium/: Nong Khai Aquarium, also called the Sirindhorn Aquarium, has a 34-metre sloping tunnel from marine tanks down to Mekong River fish. It is run by Khon Kaen University’s Nong Khai Campus.
/en/attractions/phuket-aquarium/: Phuket Aquarium at Cape Panwa is a research-run aquarium with an underwater tunnel, touch pool and daily diver feeding at 11:00. Open 08:30–16:30; it is a different place from Aquaria Phuket.
/en/attractions/phuket-old-town/: Phuket Old Town has Sino-Portuguese shophouses from the tin-mining era, Peranakan heritage, street murals and Thai Hua Museum. Try Hokkien noodles and apong, and catch Lard Yai market on Sundays.
/en/attractions/safari-world/: Safari World Bangkok pairs a drive-through Safari Park of giraffes, zebras and rhinos with a walk-through Marine Park of shows. Closed Mondays; weekday and weekend hours and show times differ.
/en/attractions/sea-life-bangkok/: SEA LIFE Bangkok Ocean World is an indoor aquarium in Siam Paragon with an Ocean Tunnel, Shark Walk and penguins. Open 10:00–20:00; see shark and penguin feeding times included with admission.
/en/attractions/taling-chan-floating-mar: Taling Chan Floating Market in Bangkok runs weekends and holidays 07:00–17:00, with dining rafts by the canal serving seafood, boat noodles and som tam. Canal boat tours are a separate activity.
/en/attractions/waghor-aquarium/: Waghor Aquarium at King Mongkut’s Science Park in Prachuap Khiri Khan shows six aquatic zones from rivers and mangroves to the sea, with a glass tunnel. Exhibitions run 09:00–15:45.
/en/attractions/wat-arun/: Wat Arun, Bangkok’s Temple of Dawn, rises on the Chao Phraya’s west bank. Open daily 08:00–18:00 with 200-baht entry for foreigners; reach it on foot from Itsaraphap MRT or by ferry from Tha Tien.
/en/attractions/wat-pho/: Wat Pho in Bangkok houses the 46-metre Reclining Buddha with 108 mother-of-pearl designs on its feet. Open 08:30–20:00, admission 300 baht, near Sanam Chai MRT; traditional massage costs extra.
/en/attractions/wat-phra-kaew/: Wat Phra Kaew, the Temple of the Emerald Buddha, sits inside Bangkok’s Grand Palace. The 500-baht palace ticket covers the temple; sales run 08:30–15:30 and online tickets open a month ahead.
/en/attractions/wat-phra-mahathat-nakhon: Wat Phra Mahathat in Nakhon Si Thammarat is southern Thailand’s great relic temple, centred on a gold-topped reliquary chedi. Learn its layout, maritime Buddhist roots and the chedi-wrapping rite.
/en/attractions/wat-phra-si-sanphet/: Wat Phra Si Sanphet in Ayutthaya is known for three bell-shaped chedis in a row, each holding the remains of an Ayutthaya king. Explore the former palace site and its ceremonial hall foundations.
/en/attractions/wat-phra-singh/: Wat Phra Singh in Chiang Mai’s Old City houses the Phra Singh Buddha in Lai Kham Viharn, with 19th-century murals of local tales. Open 07:00–22:00; admission is 50 baht for some halls.
/en/attractions/wat-phra-yai-samui/: Wat Phra Yai, Koh Samui’s Big Buddha temple, stands on Koh Fan, reached by a stone causeway. The golden seated Buddha, built in 1972, is about 12 metres tall and still a place of worship.
/en/attractions/wat-plai-laem/: Wat Plai Laem on Koh Samui centres on a pond with a white, many-armed Guanyin statue about 20 metres high and a smiling Phra Sangkatchai figure. Cross the bridges and pair it with the Big Buddha.
/en/attractions/wat-rong-khun/: Wat Rong Khun, the White Temple in Chiang Rai, is a contemporary artwork by Chalermchai Kositpipat. Open 08:00–17:00 with 200-baht admission, about 14 km from the city centre.
/en/attractions/wat-rong-suea-ten/: Wat Rong Suea Ten, Chiang Rai’s Blue Temple, pairs a vivid blue hall with a great naga at its entrance. It is about 4 km from town towards the airport, open 07:00–20:00 and free to visit for worship.
/en/attractions/wat-si-chum-sukhothai/: Wat Si Chum in Sukhothai frames the 15-metre Phra Achana Buddha through a narrow gap in 3-metre-thick walls. It lies in the northwestern zone outside the walled centre, open 08:30–17:00.
/en/attractions/wat-suthat/: Wat Suthat in Bangkok’s old city sits by the red Giant Swing, with murals, carved doors and an 8-metre Sukhothai-era bronze Buddha. Temple entry is 100 baht; the museum opens Friday to Sunday.
/en/attractions/wat-yai-chai-mongkhon/: Wat Yai Chai Mongkhon in Ayutthaya is known for a great chedi marking King Naresuan’s 1592 victory and a Reclining Buddha by the entrance. Founded in 1357; open 08:00–17:00, admission 40 baht.
/en/attractions/wualai-saturday-market/: Wua Lai Saturday Walking Street in Chiang Mai fills the silversmiths’ road south of Chiang Mai Gate from about 17:00 to 22:00. Shop silver, lacquerware and hill-tribe textiles, then eat grilled fish.
/en/attractions/yaowarat-chinatown/: Yaowarat, Bangkok’s Chinatown, mixes gold shops, Chinese temples, Chaozhou-style seafood restaurants and dried-goods grocers. Wander into its lanes and Vanich Road’s wholesale market.
/en/beaches/chaweng/: Chaweng Beach on Ko Samui’s east coast is a long curve of white sand backed by plenty of hotels. Find how to reach it, how Chaweng Noi differs, and the flag and lifeguard rules for swimming.
/en/beaches/cities/ko-chang/: Compare Ko Chang beaches on the west coast: White Sand Beach (Hat Sai Khao) with shops and restaurants close by, or broad, palm-lined Klong Prao to the south. Map, access and red-flag advice.
/en/beaches/cities/pattaya/: Compare Pattaya beaches: central Pattaya Beach along Beach Road with hotels and shopping, or Jomtien’s long coast to the south. See the beach map, road access and swimming flag guidance.
/en/beaches/cities/phuket/: Compare Phuket beaches on the west coast: lively Patong with food and shopping, long white-sand Karon, and compact Kata Yai. Use the beach map and check access and red-flag swimming rules.
/en/beaches/hua-hin/: Hua Hin Beach runs beside the royal retreat town in Prachuap Khiri Khan. Plan a seaside walk, ask about horse rides and prices on the day, and follow flag rules before swimming.
/en/beaches/jomtien/: Jomtien Beach is the long coast south of central Pattaya, lined with hotels and restaurants. Learn how to avoid ending up at Jomtien Bus Terminal, where water sports run and when not to swim.
/en/beaches/karon/: Karon Beach on Phuket’s west coast is a long stretch of white sand north of Kata. Know Karon Yai from hotel-access Karon Noi, plan a walk and a meal, and skip swimming when waves run high.
/en/beaches/kata/: Kata Beach (Kata Yai) is a compact curved bay on Phuket’s west coast, south of Karon, with hotels, bars and shops. Check how it differs from Kata Noi and where to swim away from surfing areas.
/en/beaches/klong-prao/: Klong Prao Beach on Ko Chang’s west coast is a broad palm-lined sandy shore south of White Sand. See how to reach hotels set back from the road and why you should not swim at rocky Laem Chai Chet.
/en/beaches/lamai/: Lamai Beach on Ko Samui’s east coast, south of Chaweng, is a palm-lined curve of sand. Some sections have deep water and strong waves, so read the advice on swimming with children before you go.
/en/beaches/patong/: Patong Beach is Phuket’s lively west-coast bay with hotels, restaurants and shops right behind the sand. Find road access, where to swim away from boats and water sports, and red-flag rules.
/en/beaches/wong-duean/: Ao Wong Duean is a crescent-shaped white-sand bay on Ko Samet. Learn how to book a boat from Ban Phe direct to the bay or via Na Dan Pier, and how to swim safely away from boat areas.
/en/cameras/chaam-thew-talay/: Cha-am Thew Talay live cam: see CCTV-style photographs of the Thew Talay area that refresh every few minutes. Each still shows its capture time, so you can check the sky before a Cha-am trip.
/en/cameras/chainat-chao-phraya/: Chai Nat Chao Phraya River live cam: a CCTV view of the river and dam area listed by Webcamera24. See inland Thai scenery away from the beaches; the original operator is not confirmed.
/en/cameras/chiangmai-weather-view/: Chiang Mai live cam and weather view: choose among the city’s public CCTV cameras and refreshed photos on EaseWeather to check the local sky. Each image names its area and capture time.
/en/cameras/chiangrai-mae-yao/: Chiang Rai Ban Mae Yao live cam: a CCTV view described as northern mountains and temples, listed by Webcamera24. Preview hill scenery rather than sea views; exact temple location is unconfirmed.
/en/cameras/chiangrai-wat-thep/: Chiang Rai Wat Thep Bun Yuen live cam: a public CCTV listing showing the temple and surrounding mountains in northern Thailand. It opens on Webcamera24 and does not show visitor entrances.
/en/cameras/huahin-centara/: Hua Hin Beach live cam from Centara Grand Beach Resort: watch the shore and sea in front of the hotel on this CCTV-style YouTube stream, and switch to the KBA kite school view of the same beach.
/en/cameras/huahin-kba/: Hua Hin live cam from Kiteboarding Asia (KBA): a CCTV-style view of the sea and sky off Hua Hin Beach. Preview wind and water, but check the school’s schedule before planning a kitesurf lesson.
/en/cameras/krabi-ao-nang-coast/: Krabi Ao Nang live cam: a CCTV coastal radar view shared by Thai agency GISTDA, labelled NANG OUT, showing the sea and sky off Ao Nang. It cannot confirm boat trips to Railay or nearby islands.
/en/cameras/lanta-hat-lant/: Koh Lanta live cam: a CCTV sea view of the island listed as Hat Lant on Webcamera24. Preview Koh Lanta’s water before travelling, noting the exact beach and operator are not confirmed.
/en/cameras/nakhon-cha-uat/: Nakhon Si Thammarat live cam of the Cha-uat River: a CCTV riverside view listed by Webcamera24, offering southern Thai river scenery instead of beaches. Exact filming point is unconfirmed.
/en/cameras/pathum-chao-phraya/: Pathum Thani live cam on the Chao Phraya: a CCTV view of the river and riverside town buildings, listed by camera aggregator Tufaq. See an urban river setting just north of Bangkok.
/en/cameras/pattaya-beach-panorama/: Pattaya Beach live cam: a wide SkylineWebcams panorama of the shoreline and Gulf water, like a CCTV overview of the bay. Get a feel for the city’s seafront before your trip.
/en/cameras/phangan-sanskara/: Koh Phangan Haad Rin live cam: a CCTV-style YouTube stream from House of Sanskara facing the sea at Haad Rin Beach. Watch waves reach the shore and check the sky before your island trip.
/en/cameras/phuket-cape-panwa/: Phuket Cape Panwa live cam: a CCTV-style view of quiet NĀMA Bay from the beach in front of NĀMA Freediving, looking out to the horizon. Weather here may differ from the rest of Phuket.
/en/cameras/phuket-karon-marina/: Phuket Karon Beach live cam from Marina Phuket Resort: a CCTV-style view of the southern end of Karon’s long white sand, with waves and sky. Compare it with Patong and Kata camera views.
/en/cameras/phuket-kata-surf/: Phuket Kata Beach live cam photos from SSS Phuket: CCTV-style images of the sea and incoming waves that refresh periodically. Check the capture time and always follow beach flags before surfing.
/en/cameras/phuket-patong-panorama/: Phuket Patong Bay live cam: a CCTV panorama over town buildings and greenery to the sea, via a public Ivideon player on Webcamtaxi. See Patong’s urban surroundings along with the bay.
/en/cameras/phuket-patong-tower/: Phuket Patong Beach live cam from the 15th floor of Patong Tower: a CCTV-style view over the curving shore and Andaman Sea, with skies that change colour around sunset.
/en/cameras/samet-cocoon/: Koh Samet live cam near Na Dan Pier: The Cocoon Hostel shares a CCTV-style view across the sea towards the mainland. Preview waves and clouds, but use real sailing information for ferries.
/en/cameras/samui-bang-rak/: Koh Samui Bang Rak Beach live cam: a SkylineWebcams CCTV-style view of the north coast shore and sea. Use it to tell Bang Rak apart from Lamai or Crystal Bay when choosing where to stay.
/en/cameras/samui-banyan-tree/: Koh Samui live cam from Banyan Tree Samui: an elevated CCTV-style view from the resort hillside over the bay and beach. Get a broad picture of the shore rather than close-up waves.
/en/cameras/samui-baobab/: Koh Samui Lamai Beach live cam from Baobab restaurant: a close-to-the-water CCTV-style view of sand and breaking waves on Lamai’s palm-lined bay. A Black Pearl camera shows the same beach.
/en/cameras/samui-black-pearl/: Koh Samui Lamai Beach live cam from Black Pearl: watch waves roll towards the shore on this CCTV-style YouTube stream. Compare it with the Baobab camera facing the same beach.
/en/cameras/samui-bophut-beach/: Koh Samui Bophut Beach live cam: a SkylineWebcams CCTV-style view of the island’s northern coast and the water in front of Bophut. Check the original page for current broadcast status.
/en/cameras/samui-choengmon/: Koh Samui Choeng Mon Beach live cam: a CCTV-style view of the northeast coast, its shoreline and approaching waves. Use it to tell Choeng Mon apart from Bophut and Bang Rak before booking.
/en/cameras/samui-crystal-bay/: Koh Samui Crystal Bay live cam from Crystal Bay Yacht Club: a close CCTV-style view of white sand and waves at the bay also called Thongtakian. Watch it on YouTube or in the page player.
/en/cameras/samui-crystal-beach/: Koh Samui Silver Beach live cam, listed as Crystal Bay Beach Cam: a SamuiWebcam CCTV-style view of the sea and shore around Silver Beach, opened via Webcamtaxi’s page.
/en/cameras/samui-two-palms/: Koh Samui Bang Po Beach live cam from Two Palms: a close CCTV-style YouTube view of the shore and sea at Bang Po. Preview this part of the coast if you are thinking of staying there.
/en/cameras/tao-island-skyline/: Koh Tao live cam: a SkylineWebcams CCTV-style view from a beach over a bay with islands beyond the water. Preview the island’s scenery, then choose your actual beach and route separately.
/en/coupons/: ThaiLiveNow Deals gathers official offers for travel in Thailand in one place, linking directly to the provider’s own pages, such as the Grab website and its app listing on Google Play.
/en/destinations/: Thailand travel guide hub: check entry rules, TDAC and visa types, compare weather by month, and choose between Bangkok, Chiang Mai, Chiang Rai and island destinations for your trip.
/en/entry/tdac/: How to complete Thailand’s TDAC on your phone: use the free official site within three days of arrival, enter passport details in English, choose Arrival Card, then save and edit your submission.
/en/entry/visa/: Thailand visa types explained: how visa exemption, TDAC and visas differ, and which category fits tourism, work, study, retirement, the DTV or Long-Term Resident stays, applied via Thai e-Visa.
/en/food-delivery/: Food delivery in Thailand for travellers: compare GrabFood, LINE MAN, ShopeeFood and Robinhood, set your hotel address and map pin, check the final total and ask reception where to collect orders.
/en/food-delivery/grabfood/: GrabFood Thailand guide: order through the Food menu in the Grab app, pay by cash or Thai or foreign card (foreign cards carry a 3% fee), get meals to your hotel and cancel orders correctly.
/en/food-delivery/line-man/: LINE MAN Thailand food delivery: sign in with your LINE ID, open the food menu, match your hotel address and map pin, review delivery fees at checkout, and report missing items through the order.
/en/food-delivery/robinhood/: Robinhood food delivery covers Bangkok and nearby areas. Enter your hotel address to see restaurants that deliver, check the total with delivery fees, and see how room delivery and payment work.
/en/food-delivery/shopeefood/: ShopeeFood Thailand: order meals from the ShopeeFood menu in the Thai Shopee app, which supports English. Set your hotel pin, check fees at checkout and keep food orders apart from shopping orders.
/en/food/: Thai food guide to Pad Thai, Tom Yum Kung, green and massaman curry, som tam and mango sticky rice: what each tastes like and how to eat it, plus city food, street snacks and Thai fruit.
/en/rooftops/: Thailand rooftops and viewpoints: compare 44 rooftop bars, restaurants and observation decks in Bangkok, Chiang Mai, Phuket, Pattaya, Koh Samui and Phi Phi, with hours, age rules and booking terms.
/en/rooftops/abar-rooftop/: ABar Rooftop at Bangkok Marriott Marquis Queen’s Park on Sukhumvit 22 is an outdoor gin and cocktail bar above the city lights. Open daily 17:00–01:00; see the taxi phrase and access tips.
/en/rooftops/above-eleven/: Above Eleven on the 33rd floor of Fraser Suites Sukhumvit serves Peruvian-Japanese Nikkei food and Pisco Sours with DJ music, plus Wednesday salsa nights. Open 17:00–02:00 every day.
/en/rooftops/akara-sky-hanuman/: Akara Sky Hanuman is a Thai mythology-themed sky bar on the 61st floor of One City Centre in Bangkok, open 17:00–02:00. Learn how the bar differs from the observation area and night market.
/en/rooftops/alfresco-64/: Alfresco 64 is a yacht-inspired outdoor whisky bar on the 64th floor of lebua at State Tower in Bangkok, with DJ music. Open 17:00–00:30 for ages 20 and over only; smart casual dress code.
/en/rooftops/attic-by-octave/: ATTIC by Octave is a hidden-bar-style space on the 47th floor of Bangkok Marriott Hotel Sukhumvit, pairing Sukhumvit views with Mexican-inspired drinks and bar bites. Reserve via the booking link.
/en/rooftops/baba-nest/: Baba Nest at Sri Panwa on Phuket’s Cape Panwa is a reservation-only sunset bar ringed by an infinity pool. Open 17:00–20:00, with a minimum spend of 3,000 baht for non-resident guests.
/en/rooftops/baiyoke-observatory/: Baiyoke Sky Observatory in Pratunam, Bangkok, has a 77th floor viewing area and an 84th floor revolving deck at Baiyoke Sky Hotel. Open daily 10:00–22:00; see the taxi address and access tips.
/en/rooftops/barbu-pattaya/: BARBÙ on the 24th floor of Siam@Siam Design Hotel Pattaya serves Mediterranean sharing dishes with city views. Families with children are welcome, unlike the adults-only Skybar on the 27th floor.
/en/rooftops/brewski-rooftop/: Brewski is a craft beer rooftop bar on floors 29–30 of Radisson Blu Plaza Bangkok, pairing beer and bar snacks with Sukhumvit views. Open daily 17:00–01:00; arrive early for sunset.
/en/rooftops/char-rooftop/: CHAR Rooftop Bar on the 26th floor of Hotel Indigo Bangkok Wireless Road offers signature cocktails and live music above central Bangkok. Note that CHAR Restaurant on the 25th floor is separate.
/en/rooftops/cities/bangkok/: Bangkok rooftop bars and viewpoints: compare 30 venues, from Sky Bar and Sirocco at lebua to Sky Beach, Mahanakhon SkyWalk and Baiyoke, with opening hours, age limits, dress codes and reservations.
/en/rooftops/cities/bangkok/page/2/: Page 2 of Bangkok rooftops and viewpoints: browse more of the city’s 30 venues, such as CHAR on Wireless Road, Brewski, Sky on 20, Spire at Dusit Thani and SEEN by the river, with access details.
/en/rooftops/cities/chiang-mai/: Chiang Mai rooftops and viewpoints: HONG’s Sky Bar at InterContinental The Mae Ping looks towards Doi Suthep, while Wat Phra That Doi Suthep offers a temple terrace view over the whole city.
/en/rooftops/cities/pattaya/: Pattaya rooftops and viewpoints: compare Horizon at Hilton Pattaya, adults-only Skybar Summer Club, family-friendly BARBÙ, The Portrait of Voyage Sky Bar and the Phra Tamnak hill viewpoint.
/en/rooftops/cities/phi-phi/: Phi Phi Islands rooftops and viewpoints: one venue is listed, the hilltop Viewpoint 2 on Phi Phi Don, overlooking the bay and village. Use the island map and detail page to plan your visit.
/en/rooftops/cities/phuket/: Phuket rooftops for sunset: compare Baba Nest at Sri Panwa, Sizzle at Avista Hideaway, Twilight Sky over Kata, Vanilla Sky at Kamala and The Surface in Patong, with booking and access details.
/en/rooftops/cities/samui/: Koh Samui rooftops: STAR by Silavadee sits atop Silavadee Pool Spa Resort above Lamai Bay, serving Western dishes and cocktails, with four sunken tables set in its infinity pool. See booking details.
/en/rooftops/cocoa-xo/: Cocoa XO at Centara Grand at CentralWorld in Bangkok pairs handmade chocolates with cognac cocktails and city views. Open daily 16:00–01:00, for ages 20 and over only, a sweet stop after dinner.
/en/rooftops/cru-champagne-bar/: CRU Champagne Bar on the 59th floor of Centara Grand at CentralWorld serves champagne and oysters above Bangkok. Open daily 17:00–01:00, for guests aged 20 and over; come for sunset.
/en/rooftops/distil-lebua/: For premium spirits and cigars in Bangkok, Distil by lebua offers a sky-high lounge on State Tower’s 64th floor. Take time choosing drinks with friends; adults 20 and over only, smart casual dress.
/en/rooftops/doi-suthep-viewpoint/: Wat Phra That Doi Suthep viewpoint combines the golden pagoda with a terrace view over Chiang Mai. Agree the fare before taking a red songthaew, then climb the stairs or ride the cable car up.
/en/rooftops/flute-lebua/: Flûte by lebua is an open-air Bollinger champagne bar on the 64th floor of State Tower in Bangkok, with oysters, caviar and live jazz except Mondays. Open 17:00–00:30; children 7+ with an adult.
/en/rooftops/hongs-sky-bar/: HONG’s Sky Bar at InterContinental Chiang Mai The Mae Ping is a rooftop terrace facing Doi Suthep. Open 16:00–24:00; book via the hotel, arrive on time, and note it may close in rain.
/en/rooftops/horizon-pattaya/: Horizon Rooftop Restaurant & Bar on the 34th floor of Hilton Pattaya overlooks Pattaya Bay. Book a table on Hilton’s dining page and arrive around sunset for dinner and cocktails.
/en/rooftops/iris-wild-iris/: IRIS & WILD IRIS on the 29th–30th floors of SO/ Bangkok overlooks Lumphini Park with Italian dining, aperitifs and DJ music. Open from 17:00 daily, until 01:00 on Fridays and Saturdays.
/en/rooftops/lebua-no3/: Gin, vodka and caviar are the focus at lebua No. 3, a modern bar 52 floors up in State Tower, Bangkok. Plan an unhurried adults’ evening: guests must be 20 or older, and the bar closes at 00:30.
/en/rooftops/mahanakhon-skywalk/: Mahanakhon SkyWalk in Bangkok has a 74th floor indoor deck, a 78th floor outdoor deck and a glass floor 310 m up. Open daily 10:00–24:00; book a time slot online and walk from BTS Chong Nonsi Exit 3.
/en/rooftops/octave-rooftop/: Octave Rooftop Lounge & Bar tops Bangkok Marriott Hotel Sukhumvit in Thong Lo, with food, drinks and 360-degree city views. Open daily 17:00–02:00, smart casual, with reservations available.
/en/rooftops/pastel-rooftop/: Pastel Rooftop Bar on the 22nd floor of Aira Hotel Bangkok on Sukhumvit Soi 11 pairs Mediterranean dishes and cocktails with live music. Open daily 17:00–01:00; check the events schedule.
/en/rooftops/phi-phi-viewpoint-2/: Phi Phi Don Viewpoint 2 is a hilltop lookout over Ko Phi Phi Don’s sea and village. Check the route from your accommodation before setting out, and leave time to take in the view and photographs.
/en/rooftops/phra-tamnak-viewpoint/: Phra Tamnak Mountain Viewpoint sits on the hill between south Pattaya and Jomtien, overlooking the curving beach and city. Take a Grab or Bolt up, stay for sunset and arrange your ride down.
/en/rooftops/portrait-voyage-sky-bar/: The Portrait of Voyage Sky Bar is an outdoor bar on the 33rd floor of Grande Centre Point Voyage Pattaya with sea views. Open daily 11:30–24:00; best for cocktails at sunset rather than a full meal.
/en/rooftops/red-sky-bar/: Red Sky Bar on the 56th floor of Centara Grand at CentralWorld in Bangkok offers cocktails and light bites under its arch with an open city panorama. Open daily 16:00–01:00; come before sunset.
/en/rooftops/red-sky-restaurant/: Red Sky Restaurant on the 55th floor of Centara Grand at CentralWorld serves European dishes, steaks and seafood with Bangkok night views. Dinner runs daily 17:00–01:00, with table booking.
/en/rooftops/seen-riverside/: SEEN Restaurant & Bar on floors 26–27 of Avani+ Riverside Bangkok overlooks the Chao Phraya River, with indoor and outdoor spaces, food, drinks and DJ music. See the taxi address and access.
/en/rooftops/sin-rooftop/: SIN Rooftop Bar is the outdoor bar on the 27th floor of Avani+ Riverside Bangkok, overlooking the Chao Phraya and city lights. Open 17:00–01:00 and separate from SEEN Restaurant in the same hotel.
/en/rooftops/sirocco/: Sirocco by lebua serves Mediterranean dinners on an outdoor terrace beneath the golden dome on the 63rd floor of State Tower in Bangkok. Reserve ahead and walk from BTS Saphan Taksin or take a Grab.
/en/rooftops/sizzle-rooftop/: Sizzle Rooftop Restaurant & Bar at Avista Hideaway Phuket Patong looks over the Andaman Sea and forested hills. The bar opens 17:30 and the restaurant 18:00, so plan for drinks or dinner.
/en/rooftops/sky-bar/: Sky Bar by lebua on the 64th floor of State Tower overlooks Bangkok’s Chao Phraya beside the golden dome, home of the Hangovertini. Walk-in only, one drink minimum, smart casual, children 7+.
/en/rooftops/sky-beach/: Sky Beach tops King Power Mahanakhon in Bangkok, pairing city views with cocktails, casual American food and DJ music. Open daily 10:00–24:00, all ages welcome, seats first come, first served.
/en/rooftops/sky-on-20/: Sky on 20 on the 26th floor of Novotel Bangkok Sukhumvit 20 serves cocktails, pizza and crab bruschetta over the city lights. Open daily 17:00–01:00, with DJ music on Friday and Saturday nights.
/en/rooftops/skybar-summer-club/: Skybar Summer Club on the 27th floor of Siam@Siam Design Hotel Pattaya combines Gulf of Thailand views, a two-level pool, cocktails and live DJs. Admission is for ages 18 and over only.
/en/rooftops/spectrum-lounge-bar/: Spectrum Lounge & Bar at Hyatt Regency Bangkok Sukhumvit offers dinner and live music on the 29th floor and an outdoor DJ cocktail bar on the 30th. Open 17:30–01:00; no flip-flops or sportswear.
/en/rooftops/spire-rooftop/: Spire Rooftop Bar on the 39th floor of Dusit Thani Bangkok serves Tropic City cocktails beneath the hotel’s golden spire. Open 17:00–01:00; guests under 20 may visit until 19:00, smart casual.
/en/rooftops/star-silavadee/: STAR by Silavadee on Koh Samui is a rooftop restaurant and bar above Lamai Bay with four sunken tables in an infinity pool. Open 17:30–23:00; book on the venue page and ask staff for the way up.
/en/rooftops/surface-patong/: After a Patong beach day, The Surface Restaurant & Bar on La Flora Resort’s rooftop offers cocktails and dinner above Patong Bay and the Andaman Sea. Arrange return transport if staying late.
/en/rooftops/threesixty-rooftop/: ThreeSixty Rooftop Bar on the 31st floor of Millennium Hilton Bangkok looks over the Chao Phraya River and skyline. Open 17:00–01:00 daily; come at sunset to watch riverfront lights appear.
/en/rooftops/tichuca-rooftop/: Tichuca Rooftop Bar on the 46th floor of Bangkok’s T-One Building mixes plants, city views, house music DJs and creative cocktails for a lively evening out with friends. See the taxi address.
/en/rooftops/twilight-sky/: Twilight Sky Restaurant & Bar at The SIS Kata Resort (adults only) overlooks Kata Beach and the Andaman Sea. Book by phone for sunset drinks and dinner, with live music and steak on Thursdays.
/en/rooftops/vanilla-sky/: Vanilla Sky Bar & Gastro Pub at Cape Sienna, Phuket, looks over Kamala Bay at sunset. Try a Smoky Cinnamon cocktail or draught beer with charcoal-grilled food; open daily from 17:00.
/en/rooftops/yao-rooftop/: Yao Rooftop Bar at Bangkok Marriott Hotel The Surawongse offers dim sum, cocktails and alcohol-free drinks in Chinese-inspired surroundings with old and new Bangkok views. Open daily from 17:00.
/en/transport/: Getting around Thailand: a transport hub linking guides to Bangkok rail and stations, bus terminals, boats and piers, trains, domestic flights, taxis, motorcycle taxis and tuk-tuks (in Korean).
/en/travel-seasons/rainy-dry/: Thailand’s rainy and dry seasons by region: most areas are wet mid-May to mid-October, while Koh Samui peaks late in the year. Compare Phuket and Samui rainfall and plan for rainy days.
/en/beaches/cities/hua-hin/: Hua Hin beaches compared: the town beach beside this royal retreat town and Khao Takiab to the south. Combine a seaside walk with hill scenery, treating the temple and sand as separate stops.
/en/beaches/cities/ko-samet/: Ko Samet beaches compared: white-sand Sai Kaew and the crescent bay of Ao Wong Duean. Arrange your boat from Ban Phe on the mainland and your arrival pier first, then the onward trip to the beach.
/en/beaches/cities/samui/: Ko Samui beaches compared: Chaweng and Lamai on the east coast. Both have accommodation and restaurants, but their sand and seabed differ, so weigh scenery and swimming conditions together.
/en/food/traditions/: Traditional Thai food by region: how the staples and seasonings of central Thailand, the north, Isan and the south differ, which dishes to try first and what to know before your first order.
/en/food/street-food/: Thai street food guide to roti, taeng mo pan watermelon shakes, roti sai mai, sai krok Isan sausage and Hat Yai fried chicken, and what to check on a stall's menu and prices before you order.
/en/food/fruit-prices/: Thai fruit prices explained: what to compare when fruit is sold by the kg, bunch, piece or tray, with Bangkok retail prices from the Department of Internal Trade and buying tips for six cities.
/en/food/fruits/: Thai fruit by month: a January to December calendar for 16 fruits, such as mango in March–May and pomelo in October–December, with taste, how to eat each and Bangkok retail prices.
/en/food/cities/bangkok/: Bangkok food guide to five dishes that are easy to choose first: Pad Thai, Tom Yum Kung, green curry, massaman curry and mango sticky rice, with tips for solo and group meals and fruit prices.
/en/food/cities/chiang-mai/: Chiang Mai food guide to northern Thai dishes: khao soi curry noodles, sai ua herb sausage and nam prik ong tomato dip with sticky rice, the khantoke meal, and longan and lychee to look for.
/en/food/cities/phuket/: Phuket food guide beyond grilled seafood: mi hokkien stir-fried thick noodles, mi hun thin rice noodles and o-aew iced jelly dessert, with Chinese and Malay influences and fruit buying tips.
/en/food/cities/ayutthaya/: Ayutthaya food guide to boat noodles, grilled river prawns and roti sai mai, thin roti wrapped around sugar threads, with how river prawn prices vary by size and how to buy fruit near the ruins.
/en/food/cities/khon-kaen/: Khon Kaen food guide to Isan dishes: som tam and larb with sticky rice, sai krok Isan fermented sausage and au pla freshwater fish curry, with what to ask about plara and how to buy papaya.
/en/food/cities/hat-yai/: Hat Yai food guide to Hat Yai fried chicken with fried shallots and bak kut teh pork rib soup, the Chinese and Muslim food culture of Songkhla, and why a dish name cannot tell you if it is halal.
/en/food/dishes/pad-thai/: Pad Thai is Thailand's best-known stir-fried noodle dish with egg, tofu and tamarind sauce. Learn how it tastes, how to add lime and peanuts, and what to ask about dried shrimp if you avoid shrimp.
/en/food/dishes/tom-yum-kung/: Tom Yum Kung is a hot and sour shrimp soup scented with lemongrass, galangal and kaffir lime leaves. Learn how it tastes, how to order it with rice, and what its 2024 UNESCO listing means.
/en/food/dishes/green-curry/: Green curry, or kaeng khiao wan, is made with coconut milk, green curry paste, meat and vegetables, and it is still spicy. Learn how it tastes and how to ask about heat before you order.
/en/food/dishes/massaman/: Massaman curry is a rich Thai curry scented with cinnamon, cardamom and cloves, comparatively mild but not free of heat. Learn how it tastes and why its name cannot tell you if it is halal.
/en/food/dishes/mango-sticky-rice/: Mango sticky rice is a Thai dessert of ripe mango with coconut milk sticky rice, enjoyed after a meal. Learn how it tastes, how to eat mango and rice together and how to add the sauce slowly.
/en/food/dishes/khao-soi/: Khao soi is the northern Thai dish of egg noodles in coconut curry broth topped with crispy fried noodles. Learn how it tastes, how to choose chicken or beef, and why to eat the crisp noodles first.
/en/food/dishes/sai-ua/: Sai ua is a northern Thai sausage of pork, chilies, garlic and herbs, grilled and popular in Chiang Mai. Learn how it tastes, why to start with a small piece and how to eat it with sticky rice.
/en/food/dishes/nam-prik-ong/: Nam prik ong is a northern Thai dipping sauce of tomato, minced pork and chilies, eaten with vegetables and sticky rice. Learn how it tastes, how to pair it with sai ua and why it is not vegetarian.
/en/food/dishes/mi-hokkien/: Mi hokkien is a Phuket dish of thick yellow noodles stir-fried with seafood and sauce, shaped by Chinese food culture. Learn how it differs from mi hun and what to ask if you cannot eat seafood.
/en/food/dishes/mi-hun/: Mi hun is a Phuket dish of thin rice noodles best known with a pork rib broth, also found as mi hun ba chang. Learn how to eat the noodles and broth, and why skipping the broth does not avoid pork.
/en/food/dishes/o-aew/: O-aew is a Phuket dessert of jelly, sweet syrup and toppings served over ice, a cold break on a hot day in the old town. Learn how to spoon up ice and jelly and what to ask if you avoid ingredients.
/en/food/dishes/boat-noodles/: Boat noodles, or kuai tiao ruea, are noodles and meat in broth and famous in Ayutthaya. Learn how to choose noodles, meat and bowl size, and what to ask about meat, offal and seasoning in the broth.
/en/food/dishes/river-prawns/: Grilled river prawns are an Ayutthaya dish to share with rice. Learn why price changes with size and selling unit, how to ask if it is per prawn or by weight, and why the name does not prove origin.
/en/food/dishes/roti-sai-mai/: Roti sai mai is an Ayutthaya snack of thin roti wrapped around fine sugar threads, tied to local Muslim snack culture. Learn how it differs from ordinary roti, the pandan version and how to wrap it.
/en/food/dishes/som-tam/: Som tam is Isan's signature papaya salad, pounded with chilies and sour seasonings and eaten across Thailand. Learn how it tastes, when to ask about plara fish seasoning and how to cut the heat.
/en/food/dishes/larb/: Larb is an Isan meat salad of minced meat with toasted rice powder, lime and herbs, eaten with sticky rice. Learn how it tastes and why to order it cooked, since some larb uses raw meat.
/en/food/dishes/sai-krok-isan/: Sai krok Isan is an Isan sausage of fermented pork, rice and garlic, with a tang that sets it apart from northern sai ua. Learn how it tastes and how to eat the raw chilies served with it slowly.
/en/food/dishes/au-pla/: Au pla is a spicy, salty freshwater fish curry presented as a local dish of Khon Kaen. Learn how it differs from som tam and larb, what to ask about the fish and heat, and how to watch for bones.
/en/food/dishes/hat-yai-chicken/: Hat Yai fried chicken is a signature dish of Hat Yai, seasoned with garlic, coriander root and white pepper, with fried shallots. Learn how to eat it and why chicken alone is no halal proof.
/en/food/dishes/bak-kut-teh/: Bak kut teh is a Chinese-descended pork rib soup simmered with herbs, found in the Songkhla area. Learn how it tastes, why it is not called a Hat Yai original, and why it is not for pork avoiders.
/en/food/dishes/roti/: Thai roti is a street snack of cooked thin dough with sweet sauces like condensed milk or chocolate, sometimes with banana. Learn how to order it and how it differs from roti sai mai.
/en/food/dishes/watermelon-shake/: Taeng mo pan, the Thai watermelon shake, is watermelon blended with water and ice and sold as a street drink. Learn how it tastes, how to compare cup sizes and how to ask for less sugar.
/en/food/fruits/mango/: Mango in Thailand has a main season of March–May, with Nam Dok Mai and Maha Chanok varieties. Learn how ripe and green mango taste, how to cut it, and how price units differ for fruit and trays.
/en/food/fruits/durian/: Durian in Thailand has a main season of April–August, with Monthong, Chanee and Kan Yao varieties. Learn how it tastes, how to start small, and why to ask if the kg price includes the husk.
/en/food/fruits/mangosteen/: Mangosteen in Thailand has a main season of April–August. Learn how it tastes, how to open it, and why the Bangkok price of 40–60 baht per kg is not the weight of the flesh, since the skin is thick.
/en/food/fruits/rambutan/: Rambutan in Thailand is listed for harvest in April–August, and Nasan Rong Rian of Surat Thani is a regional GI fruit. Learn how it tastes, how to peel it and the Bangkok price of 50–60 baht per kg.
/en/food/fruits/longan/: Longan in Thailand has a main season of June–August, and Lamphun Biao Kiao longan is a regional GI fruit. Learn how it tastes, how to peel it, and the Bangkok price of 50–60 baht per kg.
/en/food/fruits/lychee/: Lychee in Thailand is listed for harvest in April–June, and Samut Songkhram Kom lychee is a regional GI fruit. Learn how to peel it, how it tastes, and why lychee drinks may not match fresh fruit.
/en/food/fruits/longkong/: Longkong in Thailand is listed for harvest in May–September, and Tha Yong Mat longkong is a regional GI fruit. Learn how it differs from longan, how to peel it and the Bangkok price of 40–50 baht/kg.
/en/food/fruits/pomelo/: Pomelo in Thailand has a main season of October–December and looks like a huge grapefruit. Learn how to peel it, why a prepared tray is easier, and why fruit and trays are hard to compare by weight.
/en/food/fruits/pineapple/: Pineapple in Thailand has a main season of April–July, and Si Thong pineapple of Trat is a regional GI fruit. Learn how it tastes, how to eat it, and the Bangkok price, 30–32 baht per kg.
/en/food/fruits/banana/: Thai banana is a fruit to enjoy all year, often priced by the bunch, and Kamphaeng Phet Kluai Khai is a regional GI fruit. See what to check on a bunch and Nam Wa at 40–50 baht per bunch in Bangkok.
/en/food/fruits/coconut/: Young coconut in Thailand is harvested all year, and the fragrant Nam Hom of Ban Phaeo is a regional GI fruit. Learn how to drink the water and eat the flesh, and why bottled water is priced apart.
/en/food/fruits/watermelon/: Watermelon in Thailand is harvested all year and enjoyed as taeng mo pan, blended with ice. Learn how to eat it, why fruit, slices and shake are priced apart, and the Bangkok price, 25–30 baht/kg.
/en/food/fruits/papaya/: Papaya in Thailand is harvested all year. Learn how ripe papaya, eaten soft and sweet, differs from the green papaya used in som tam, how to cut it, and the Bangkok price of 40–60 baht per kg.
/en/food/fruits/tamarind/: Sweet tamarind in Thailand has a main harvest listed from late December to February, and Phetchabun sweet tamarind is a regional GI fruit. Learn how to open the pod and remove fibers and seeds.
/en/food/fruits/mandarin/: Thai mandarin orange is in season October–February, and Nan golden orange is a green-skinned regional GI fruit. Learn how it tastes, why green is not unripe and the Bangkok price, 60–65 baht/kg.
/en/food/fruits/marian-plum/: Mayongchid, or Marian plum, is a plum mango family fruit with a Nakhon Nayok harvest listed for January–March. Learn how it tastes, how to cut it and remove the seed, and why to name the variety.
